newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: ICTSI drops 11.76 pct on cargo volume.
newsitem.headline: ICTSI drops 11.76 pct on cargo volume.

text.p: International Container Terminal Services Inc (ICTSI) fell 1.50 pesos, or by 11.76 percent, to 11.25 pesos by midtrade due to the lower-than-expected cargo volume posted in the first quarter, traders said on Monday.
ICTSI reported earlier a 2.7 percent increase in container traffic to 204,529 twenty foot equivalent units (TEUs) in the first quarter of the year.
Noel Reyes, research director at Anscor Hagedorn Securities, said the growth was lower-than-expected.
"The cargo volume is not in line with the 15 to 20 percent increase the company is expecting for the year," he told Reuters.

ICTSI's lower cargo traffic in the Manila International Container Terminal (MICT) "reflects a slowdown in the economy's trade activity since a majority of the country's imports and exports pass through the MICT," Anscor said in an earlier advisory to its clients.
